question: A wholesaler offers a trade discount of 15% on a product priced at ₹8,000. The customer is also eligible for a scheme discount of 5% on the already discounted price. What is the final price the customer has to pay?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the percentage discounts into multiplying factors directly.

15% discount = 15/100 = 3/20 → Multiplying factor = (20 − 3)/20 = 17/20

5% discount = 5/100 = 1/20 → Multiplying factor = (20 − 1)/20 = 19/20

Final Price = Marked Price × Multiplier 1 × Multiplier 2

Final Price = 8000 × (17/20) × (19/20) = 8000 × 323/400 = 20 × 323 = ₹6,460

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,460.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of the product = ₹8,000

Trade discount = 15%

Scheme discount = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × [(100 − D₁)/100] × [(100 − D₂)/100]

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 15% Trade Discount = 8000 − (15/100 × 8000)

⇒ Price after Trade Discount = 8000 − 1200 = ₹6,800

⇒ Final Price after 5% Scheme Discount = 6800 − (5/100 × 6800)

⇒ Final Price = 6800 − 340 = ₹6,460

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,460.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When multiple discounts are given one after the other, the equivalent single discount can be found using the formula: Effective Discount% = x + y − (x × y)/100.

Marked Price (MP) vs Selling Price (SP)

The Marked Price is the initial labeled price. All discounts are sequentially applied to this base value. After all deductions, the final payable amount is called the Selling Price: SP = MP × (100 − D%)/100.

Multiplier Method for Percentages

Instead of calculating the discount amount and subtracting it, you can directly multiply by the remaining percentage. For example, a 15% discount means the customer pays 85% of the price, saving calculation time.
